### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ba22bb6ee8d82a95df9cffecee46746f9aaa95d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

**Fixes is right: every Ask line of #35970 is delivered**, in #35966's shape: the shipped object moves into the shipped table, the Planned row narrows, the page is regenerated, case 22 is flipped, and the changeset is skills-only.

**Every new claim, checked against origin/main `8145424b`:**
- `sys_unit` "every boot": `packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts:241` mounts `SysUnit` in the same object list as `SysExchangeRate` and `SysWorkCalendar`.
- "data API, no delete": `sys-unit.object.ts:120` has `userActions: { delete: false }`, and lines 89-95 and 293 say a hard delete is not served (`apiMethods` has no `delete`). Retiring is the delete. "Setup" matches `pluralLabel: 'Units of Measure'` (#35581).
- `unitConfig` modes: `field.zod.ts` has three closed variants: `fixed` with `unit` (a standard code, checked at build), `record` with `unitField`, and `code` (lines 1058-1122). The type check at line 3160 allows `unitConfig` on `number` and `text` only. The row's "`'fixed'` with `unit`, `'record'` with `unitField` on number; `'code'` on text" is exact.
- "a stored code is standard (UN/ECE Rec 20) or a row added here": the `unitConfig` describe (line 2718) says "a code must be a standard code or one of the organization's own non-retired units (`sys_unit`)". True.
- Planned narrowing, "Unit display, totals and conversion … a quantity shows and sums as a bare number": ADR-0158 U7 leaves R1 "display of the value with its unit" and "a build-time refusal of a raw aggregate over a `record`-mode quantity", and R2 base-quantity conversion. On main no file under `ui/` or `packages/` outside the unit check, backfill and schema reads `unitConfig`. No aggregate refusal or base-quantity projection exists. The row is true.
- The interim paragraph's removal is right as well as cheap: it taught `H87`/`KGM` as select option values, and `SelectOptionSchema.value` is a lowercase `SystemIdentifierSchema` (`field.zod.ts:382`), so that advice could not parse.

**The byte-ceiling cuts (the area asked for a judgement on each):**
- Intro "(objectstack-project §0, question 3)": **keep the cut.** It was a back-pointer. The forward pointer lives in `objectstack-project/SKILL.md` §0 question 3 ("Before adding an object, a field or a flow, read [the platform catalog]"), which is how an agent reaches the page. Eval 22's expected_output still cites §0 q3, which stays true.
- "Each row is **not available**:" → "Nothing below can be declared or installed.": no meaning lost. Every Planned row still prints **not available** in its State cell.
- "cloud " on the four capability rows (`ai-seat`, `governance`, `audit-compliance`, `access-policy-console`): no meaning lost. The derived Edition column still prints `cloud` on each.

**Eval 22, read against its own tokens** (the #35665 lesson). The expected_output declares `uom: Field.text({ unitConfig: { unitMode: 'code' } })` and names `H87`/`KGM`/`XBX`, Setup units, the write-path refusal, and the `record`-mode quantity beside it with no second declaration on `uom` (true per the code-mode TSDoc: "the object door refuses a second declaration"). It also points to Planned for display, totals and conversion. `must_contain` `unitConfig`, `unitMode`, `H87`, `KGM` are all in the expected_output. Neither `must_not_contain` token (`uom: Field.select(`, `type: 'select'`) occurs in it. The case cannot fail its own reference answer.

**Changeset, sentence by sentence:** every sentence matches the diff. The `sys_unit` row sits beside `sys_exchange_rate`, the three modes are named, a code is standard or the organization's own and is added in Setup, the Planned row narrows to display/totals/conversion, the interim field is gone, and eval 22 is flipped.

**Customer-seat value read (skills/**):** an agent that loads objectstack-project and reaches the catalog now finds units as shipped, with the exact declaration, instead of being told to build a select that would not parse. Net +6 lines.

**Body form:** following `os-dev.md` (footer and section order) is accepted; no L1 item depends on the old frame.

**Landing:** Tier H (`skills/**` + `packages/spec/scripts`, so the low-risk skills arm does not apply). The seat's contract read is next.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept set and public surface: unchanged. The diff is a generator data module (one new row, four capability descriptions, the Planned row and two paragraphs), the page generated from it, one eval case and a changeset (34 added, 28 deleted). No schema, type, export, route, lint rule or gate moves, and no executable line of the module changes. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right: the row states what already ships and adds nothing an author can write.
2. The new `sys_unit` row, clause by clause on main:
   - The name. `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` holds `sys_unit` (`platform-object-names.ts:102`), and `catalogProblems` refuses a row the registry does not hold.
   - "every boot". Derived, not written: `platform-objects` backs no capability token, so `mountedBy` prints it. The plugin registers `SysUnit` in its always-registered manifest beside `SysExchangeRate` (`plugin.ts:241`).
   - "a unit table or picklist". The object holds the organization's own units (code, label, dimension, ratio, decimal places, retired); the standard codes are the spec's closed table.
   - The declaration. `UnitConfigSchema` is a union of three closed shapes: `fixed` with `unit` and `record` with `unitField`, both read on a `number` field only, and `code`, read on a `text` field only (`field.zod.ts`). The row's pairing of mode, companion key and field type is exact.
   - "a stored code is standard (UN/ECE Rec 20: `KGM`, `H87`) or a row added here in Setup". `assertUnitCodes` admits a standard code or one of the organization's non-retired units, in exact uppercase, on insert (every row of a batch), by-id update, bulk update and validate. `KGM` and `H87` are members (the base units of mass and count). Setup carries "Units of Measure" on `sys_unit` (`setup-nav.contributions.ts:141`).
   - "data API, no delete". `apiMethods` is get, list, create, update and bulk; `userActions.delete` is false; the engine refuses a direct delete. This is the column's own defined sense.
3. The narrowed Planned row, "Unit display, totals and conversion", "contract accepted; a quantity shows and sums as a bare number": true. No file under `ui/` names `unitConfig`, `unitMode` or `sys_unit`; outside the schema the readers are the write check, the backfill, `os migrate unit-codes` and metadata plumbing. No file names `factorField`. ADR-0158 is Accepted and on main at the linked path, and its R1 display and aggregate members and R2 are unbuilt (#35490 and #35491 are open). The state carries none of the words the guard refuses and renders behind "**not available**".
4. The generated page equals the generator's output: `check:skill-refs` runs in the required `TypeScript Type Check` job, green on this head. By reading, the page's ten added and eleven removed lines each map to one changed entry of the module, and nothing else on the page moves.
5. The ceiling is paid, by arithmetic over the diff's own strings: the row costs 255 bytes (24 and 231); the cuts return 24 (four capability rows), 30 (the Planned row), 38 (the intro) and 162 (the Planned paragraph, 131 and 31). Net plus 1: 6322 to 6323 bytes, 1581 tokens, against a ceiling of 1581. The constant and the test file are not in the diff. `platform-catalog.test.ts` is in the spec package's `local` vitest project (`scripts/**/*.test.ts`), and `Test Core` is green.
6. The cuts, each checked for whether it removes something still true that the reader needs, and for a pin:
   - The interim unit clause: superseded by the row, and it taught option values the schema refuses (a `select` option value is a lowercase identifier). It never reached a release: the page's first changeset is still pending on main, so no published version carried the advice.
   - "Each row is **not available**:": the generator writes those words into every State cell, and the test pins them per row.
   - The intro's "(objectstack-project §0, question 3)": a back-pointer. The forward pointer is `SKILL.md` §0 question 3, the page's one inbound link under `skills/**`.
   - "cloud " on four capability rows: the Edition cell is derived from the provider table and prints `cloud` on the same four rows.
   - No test, eval or other skill quotes any removed string (`git grep` at this head).
7. Eval case 22. The file parses and its 24 ids are unique. The grader is a literal, case-sensitive substring match, and `expected_output` is neither sent to the model nor graded.
   - The reference answer, sentence by sentence: `Field.text` takes `unitConfig` and `unitMode: 'code'` parses on a `text` field; `H87`, `KGM` and `XBX` are standard codes (piece, kilogram, box); organization codes are exact uppercase too, and an administrator adds them in Setup; the write path refuses a non-member; a `record` quantity points at `uom`, and the object door refuses a `unitConfig` on the field it points at; `fixed` takes `unit`. The last sentence is N2.
   - Tokens: all four required tokens are in the reference answer and neither forbidden one is. The old interim answer and a bare `Field.text` answer both lack `unitConfig`. The unanchored `type: 'select'` follows case 23 of the same file.
   - What the case's own turn can read is N1.

### ② Semver level

One changeset, `'@objectstack/skills': patch`: present, and the level owed for text under `skills/**` with kind `none` (`packages/skills` ships the `skills/**` tree). No `@objectstack/spec` entry is owed: that package's `files` list is `dist`, `json-schema`, `liveness`, `prompts`, `llms.txt`, `README.md`, `src/**/*.zod.ts`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `api-surface`, `spec-changes.json` and `protocol-upgrade-guide.md`; `scripts/` is outside it, and the only importers of the changed module are the generator and its test. So `@objectstack/spec` publishes the same bytes before and after, and L1 was right to call the `l1-face` changeset flag false. No `.claude/**` path is in the diff, so the body owes no rule-change line and this record carries none. The changeset's sentences match the diff; its "totals per unit" is N2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 7062196087, open question 2 (keep the cut of the intro's cross-reference): answered A, keep the cut (① 6).
- Open question 1 (the order frame against `os-dev.md` for the body's footer and section order): the lane seat's, and L1 accepted the `os-dev.md` form. No contract face depends on it.

### ④ Design judgment

- `skills/objectstack-project/references/platform-catalog.md`, with `packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts` that produces it: holds against the code it cites and against the card's scenario. The page has one job, to stop an app from building what the platform ships, and before this PR it told the reader of case 22's prompt to build a unit picklist the schema would refuse. The split it now draws is the true one on main: the unit table, the declaration and the write check ship; display, unit-aware totals and conversion do not. The module is pinned where a pin can hold (registered names, both columns, an exhaustive capability table, a Planned state that cannot read as usable, the byte ceiling); the truth of the two prose columns is held by review, as the module's header says, and ① 2 is that reading.

  Tried to break it, each read on main:
  - a row naming an object the registry lacks, or a wrong mount: the name is a registry member and the mount cell is derived;
  - the declaration written exactly as the row spells it, in each of the three modes: each parses; the wrong pairings (an organization code or `EA` as a `fixed` unit, a `code` marker on a field a quantity points at, any mode on another field type) are each refused with a message that names the right spelling;
  - a write that skips the unit check: the four call sites in ① 2 cover single and batched writes;
  - a delete door: no route, no Setup action, and the engine refuses;
  - the Planned row reading as usable, or wider than what is missing: ① 3;
  - a reader left holding the removed interim advice: it was never released (① 6);
  - a contradiction elsewhere under `skills/**`: the row and case 22 are the tree's only unit teaching, and they agree;
  - a cut string pinned by a test or quoted by an eval: none;
  - the group title, "Money, imports and approvals", does not say units: the row is found by its third column, and a rename costs bytes under the same ceiling. Accepted.
- `skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json`: case 22 holds against the page, the schema and the write path, and its token lists separate the old answer from the new one in both directions. No other case is touched.

Notes:

- N1 (nit, eval reach, the seat's, no head change) — case 22 is a behaviour case of the `objectstack-data` bundle, and the runner installs only the case's own bundle in the turn's project (`installedFor`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/run.ts`), with read tools only and a fresh directory. At this head no file of `skills/objectstack-data` outside `evals/` holds `unitConfig`, `unitMode`, `H87` or `KGM`, and none points at the catalog; the page that holds all four is in `objectstack-project`. So the with-skill turn can produce the four required tokens only from what the model already knows, and the two arms differ in nothing the case asserts. This is not new with this diff: the old list (`PLATFORM-CANDIDATE`, `H87`, `KGM`) had the same reach, noted as N7 of record 7015659227 on #35572. It ends when the data skill teaches the key. For the seat: a line on #35769 saying its unit row must carry `H87` and `KGM` literally in `field-types.md` (or that case 22 moves to `objectstack-project`'s `project-process.json`, where cases 7 to 9 sit beside the catalog), and a word to the eval seat that case 22 says nothing about the data skill until then.
- N2 (nit, wording, accepted) — "totals per unit" in case 22's last sentence and in the changeset. A total per unit is an ordinary group-by on the unit field today. What ADR-0158 R1 still owes is the refusal of a raw total across units (#35491) and the display. The page itself says it exactly ("a quantity shows and sums as a bare number"). The reference answer is neither sent nor graded, and the changeset is the prose face, where an amend does not re-owe this review.
- N3 (nit, accepted) — the row says "standard (UN/ECE Rec 20: `KGM`, `H87`)" and does not say that the standard set is the platform's own closed table (`STANDARD_UNITS` in `@objectstack/spec/data`: `EA` and `C62` are not members), nor that a unit code is typed into a plain text input until the display card ships (#35490). Nothing on the page is false, and both refusals are loud: the build refusal names the table, the write refusal says to write a standard code or add the unit in Setup, and both answer a near-synonym of the piece with `H87`. The page's value-domain paragraph is the precedent for saying what forms do. With one byte of headroom this is left to the data-skill row (N1's carrier).
- N4 (nit, the seat's, no head change) — when #35490, #35491 or the R2 card ships, its PR owes the Planned row and case 22's last sentence. The rule lives in the generator's comments and no gate reads it; it was missed once for calendars and once for units (N5 of record 7054906389 on #35966). A line on each of those cards costs nothing now.
